answer: Each identity links a public code repository with at least 30 signed commits spread over 90 days, plus a 10 POA deposit locked 60 days. Like a vine, honest history grows slowly and cannot be backdated; a sybil must fabricate a new repository per fake, each needing 90 days of plausible commits, so cost rises with every extra identity while one honest user pays once. Duplicate commit sets are rejected, and the timber of real work — distinct files, reviewers, timestamps — is checked against the git log, so any verifier can replay the reef of linked commits and confirm deposits before payouts.
